feedback.problem: Which of the following is the graph of the function $y=-{(\frac{1}{3})}^{x-2}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
To plot the given function, we follow these steps:

- We take the curve $y={(\frac{1}{3})}^{x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13943741/assets/6dd511da4a6bab6e37383620852446da06e84207517efc23165544f823ed330f.png)

 

- Horizontally shift it by $2$ units to the right to give $y={(\frac{1}{3})}^{x-2}.$ The $y$-intercept moves from $(0,1)$ to $(2,1)$ but the horizontal asymptote stays at $y=0.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13943741/assets/4d60dc4fe52cd717370ae1eeb28dd35b0c3c8e4a4e69ff088b16e56c03be5735.png)

- Then, reflect it on the $x$-axis to give $y=-{(\frac{1}{3})}^{x-2}.$ The point $(2,1)$ moves to $(2,-1)$ and the horizontal asymptote stays at $y=0.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13943741/assets/e4b042273bfb3a6640e57c75eff3058dd177bc2d75dfdf312160a4a6c9a9de53.png)
